cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
cards.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved our museum's lost-time exhibit. You put yesterday's missing hour in this jar; I'll write the label.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Time doesn't fit in jars. Can I just write the label instead?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Reassignment denied. Use the wide-necked jar. I won't have you blaming the equipment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then what do I tell the curator when she sees it's empty?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her you're still responsible for the contents. I'll label it 'One hour, awaiting delivery' and put your name beside 'supplier'.

reason: Ground the impossible assignment in an exhibit and use B's curator question to make A preserve responsibility through a concrete public label.
